question: is the +2.5% at the BAO peaks a phase error or an amplitude error?
method: locate the local extrema of our P(k) and CAMB's P(k) in ln k and compare their positions; a phase error shifts them, an amplitude error does not
verdict: not a phase error - the first acoustic peak sits at exactly the same wavenumber in both. The residual is in amplitude/damping, not in the acoustic scale or its propagation.
why_this_does_not_pin_it_down: with 30 points over 0.015-0.45 the spacing in ln k is 0.113 against a BAO period near 0.5, i.e. 4-5 samples per oscillation. Only one peak was detected and no troughs at all, so the diagnostic is resolution-limited and cannot separate the amplitude cleanly.

what_is_therefore_excluded.acoustic_scale: the peak positions agree exactly, and r*(z*) was already validated to 4e-5 (144.4 vs CAMB 144.41 Mpc)
what_is_therefore_excluded.damping_via_opacity: kappa and its ln-a derivative perturbed by +-2% moved the peak by 0.039pp
what_is_therefore_excluded.photon_hierarchy_height: lmax_g 24 / 40 / 64 bit-identical (the RSA freezes the upper rows anyway)
what_is_therefore_excluded.time_integrator: quartering dlna_max and dlna_acoustic moved the plateau by 0.0002
what_is_therefore_excluded.gauge_and_stress_equations: z, dz, etak, sigma, adotdota, sigmadot all match CAMB line for line

state_of_the_linear_residual: twenty-plus suspects excluded and the remaining +2.5% BAO-peak excess has no identified single-point cause. It is an accumulated difference between two integrators, not a locatable bug - which is exactly why it resists the last few rounds of diagnosis.
significance_for_the_nonlinear_work: this matters because the end-to-end nonlinear call reads 3.50% against HMcode-alone's 0.88%, and the difference is this linear input. So the linear residual is now the largest single term in the nonlinear error, and it is the one thing currently without a fix.
